data.title: Nummular (discoid) eczema — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Nummular (discoid) eczema** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. What is nummular eczema?**
- Coin-shaped, well-defined eczematous plaques (papulovesicular, oozing, crusted) mainly on extensor limbs and dorsa of hands, very itchy, chronic relapsing

**Q2. Associations?**
- Xerosis (elderly men), atopy (young), staphylococcal colonisation, contact allergy (nickel, chromate), venous insufficiency, alcohol, drugs (isotretinoin, interferon), dental infection (focal infection)

**Q3. Differential diagnosis?**
- Tinea corporis (central clearing, KOH positive), psoriasis, impetigo, Bowen disease, mycosis fungoides, contact dermatitis, lichen simplex

**Q4. Treatment?**
- Emollients, potent topical steroids (ointment, occlusion), tacrolimus, treat infection (topical/oral antistaphylococcal), patch testing if recalcitrant, NB-UVB, methotrexate/azathioprine for extensive disease

## Quick spotter facts
- Coin-shaped oozing eczematous plaques on legs — nummular eczema

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Nummular eczema); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.24. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
